summary.text: Sodium chloride, or NaCl, is an ionic compound made of sodium and chloride ions in a 1:1 ratio.
As table salt it is a condiment and food preservative, and it occurs naturally as the mineral halite.
Most of the world's production goes into making chemicals, and another major use is de-icing roads in freezing weather.

facts.label: Formula
facts.value: NaCl, one sodium ion for each chloride ion

facts.label: World production
facts.value: About 250 million tonnes a year, by 2008 data

facts.label: De-icing limit
facts.value: Salt or brine becomes ineffective below -10 degrees C

facts.label: Environmental cost
facts.value: Road salt reaching fresh water could harm aquatic plants and animals

items.prompt: A road crew sprays brine on a road before snow is forecast. What does that do?

options.label: It melts the snow instantly by making the road warmer
It stops snow and ice bonding to the road surface
It makes the road surface harder and rougher
It soaks into the road and removes the need for salt

items.explain: Anti-icing with brine prevents bonding between snow-ice and the road surface, and avoids heavy use of salt after the snowfall.

items.prompt: A winter night drops to -15 degrees C and the gritting crew's salt seems to do little. What is the most likely reason?

options.label: Salt works only on roads that are already wet
The salt was mixed with sodium ferrocyanide
Salt and brine are ineffective at temperatures that low
Salt turns into a different compound in the cold

items.explain: The use of salt or brine becomes ineffective below -10 degrees C.

items.prompt: A friend says salt is just a seasoning. Which fact best shows how much more it is used for?

options.label: Most of the world's production goes into making other chemicals
Table salt comes in several shapes of crystal
Salt is hygroscopic, so it tends to clump on damp days
Salt is mined only in a single mine in England

items.explain: Salt is used in the production of many chemicals, which consumes most of the world's production, along with de-icing.

items.prompt: A water-softening unit in a hard-water home stops working well. What does it need to get going again?

options.label: A fresh supply of calcium and magnesium
A rinse of sulfuric acid
A lower water temperature
Its resin regenerated using sodium chloride

items.explain: Softeners use ion-exchange resins to remove hardness ions, and the resins are generated and regenerated using sodium chloride.

items.prompt: A town spreads rock salt on its roads every winter. What side effect might follow downstream?

options.label: It might harm aquatic life by disrupting how it regulates salt and water
It might make the streams freeze at a higher temperature
It might turn the water into a good drilling fluid
It might strip the chlorine from the water entirely

items.explain: Road salt ends up in fresh-water bodies and could harm aquatic plants and animals by disrupting their osmoregulation ability.

items.prompt: Why is a lump of rock salt described as made of two kinds of ions rather than molecules of NaCl?

options.label: It is a mixture of sodium metal and chlorine gas
It is a compound made of ions in a 1:1 ratio
It is a single huge covalent molecule
It is a metal with a sea of electrons

items.explain: Sodium chloride is an ionic compound with a 1:1 ratio of sodium and chloride ions.
